headline: Ituran: a subscription compounder priced like a hardware seller
subheadline: Recurring telematics revenue is growing faster than the market gives it credit for, and it is backed by net cash and a ~4% dividend
narrative: Ituran sells stolen-vehicle recovery and connected-car services on monthly subscriptions. Subscriptions were 76% of revenue in Q2 2026 and grew 25% year on year.
Its 2.71 million subscribers are spread across Israel, where management claims an 85–90% telematics share, Brazil, other Latin American markets, India and the US.
Car-maker (OEM) deals such as Stellantis, BMW Motorrad and Yamaha bring in subscribers without retail marketing spend, and Ituran has added roughly 40,000 a quarter.
The business is highly cash-generative: record operating cash flow of $32.2m in Q2 2026, a $10m quarterly dividend, and net cash on the balance sheet.
At about 8x EV/EBITDA and 10x EV/EBIT, the stock trades well below telematics and connected-fleet peers (medians ~13x and ~21x) despite strong margins. Our target implies ~20% upside.
market_pricing: At $48 the market values Ituran at about 8x EBITDA, 10x EBIT and 15x earnings, against peer medians of about 13x EBITDA and 21x EBIT.
The discount reflects Israeli and Brazilian country risk and currency swings (the shekel and the real).
Our DCF already adds a one-point country-risk premium to WACC. Even so, it supports about $50 per share, and the comps support more.

business.title: Telematics subscriptions across Israel and Latin America
business.subtitle: Stolen-vehicle recovery, fleet management and connected-car services, sold through insurers, car makers and directly
overview: Listed on Nasdaq; headquartered in Azour, Israel.
Revenue in Q3 2025 by region: Israel 55%, Brazil 23%, rest of world 22%.
Subscriber base: 2,711,000 at June 2026, up 163,000 year on year.
Led by co-CEOs from the founding Sheratzky family. Insiders hold about 20% of the shares.

segments.name: Subscription fees (76% of Q2 2026 revenue)
segments.text: Monthly fees for stolen-vehicle recovery, tracking, fleet management and usage-based insurance data. $80m in Q2 2026, up 25%.

segments.name: Products (24%)
segments.text: Telematics devices sold to OEMs, dealers and fleets. $25.0m in Q2 2026, up 8%. Lower margin, but each unit sold brings a subscriber.

business.source: Ituran Q2 2026 results (6-K, 12 Aug 2026); Q3 2025 earnings call
business.financials_title: Steady growth with ~21% EBIT margins and rising free cash flow
financial_points: Q2 2026: record revenue of $104.8m (+21%), EBITDA $28.5m (+24%), net income $17.3m (+29%).
Gross margin improved to 50.9% from 49.5% as high-margin subscriptions grew faster than devices.
Capital return: $10m quarterly dividend ($0.50 per share) plus buybacks.

industry.title: Vehicle telematics is moving from aftermarket boxes to factory-fitted services
industry.subtitle: Insurers, car makers and fleets all want connected-vehicle data
market: Stolen-vehicle recovery is close to essential in Brazil and Israel, where insurers often require or reward a tracking device.
Car makers increasingly fit telematics at the factory and look for a service partner to run it, which is Ituran's OEM channel.
Fleet management and usage-based insurance add more data services on top of the same device.

tailwinds.title: OEM partnerships
tailwinds.text: Stellantis, BMW Motorrad (Brazil) and Yamaha deals bring subscribers in at the factory, with no retail acquisition cost.

tailwinds.title: New services on the base
tailwinds.text: IturanMob for rental fleets launched in Brazil and is piloting in the US (Orlando, New York). Ituran also won its first multi-year big-data traffic-monitoring contract (Sep 2026).

headwinds.title: Country and FX risk
headwinds.text: Most revenue is earned in shekels and reais while Ituran reports in dollars. The swings move both earnings and the share price.

headwinds.title: Connected cars
headwinds.text: Car makers' own built-in connectivity could, over time, reduce demand for aftermarket recovery devices.

industry.source: Ituran Q3 2025 and Q2 2026 results and calls; Ituran press release 9 Sep 2026

competition.title: A dominant home market and a scale position in Brazil
competition.subtitle: High returns on equity relative to larger connected-fleet peers
points: In Israel, management claims an 85–90% telematics share, which makes it the default provider for insurers.
Profitability is high for its size: EBIT margins of about 21% and ROE of 27% in 2025.
porter: Fragmented in Latin America (local trackers, insurer-owned services); near-monopoly in Israel.
Car makers' built-in connectivity and phone-based tracking are long-term substitutes for aftermarket devices.
Low barriers for devices; high barriers for a recovery network (control centres, field teams, police links).
Hardware components are commoditised; cellular connectivity is bought from several carriers.
Insurers and OEMs negotiate hard on price, but switching a large installed base is costly.
competition.source: Ituran earnings calls (Q3 2025, Q2 2026); peer data from Yahoo Finance

theses.title: 1. Subscriptions are compounding faster than the multiple implies
theses.subtitle: The fastest-growing part of revenue is also the highest-margin part
points: Subscription revenue grew 25% year on year in Q2 2026 and is now 76% of revenue. This is recurring income with high visibility.
Net adds have held at about 40,000 a quarter for over a year, with OEM channels adding to the base.
Profit is growing faster than revenue: in Q2, EBITDA rose 24% and net income 29% on revenue up 21%.
theses.risk: Net adds slow well below 30,000 a quarter, or subscription growth falls back to single digits.
theses.source: Ituran Q2 2026 results (6-K) and earnings call

theses.title: 2. Cash returns put a floor under the stock
theses.subtitle: A ~4% dividend yield and net cash protect the downside
points: Ituran pays a $10m quarterly dividend ($0.50 per share), about a 4% yield at $48, and buys back shares as well.
Operating cash flow reached a record $32.2m in Q2 2026, comfortably covering the dividend.
Ituran holds net cash, so the dividend does not depend on borrowing, and there is room for acquisitions, which management prefers for expansion.
theses.risk: A large debt-funded acquisition, or a dividend cut to fund growth outside the core.

evidence.title: Capital return
points: The dividend was raised 25% in 2025, from $8m to $10m a quarter.

theses.title: 3. New growth levers are optional upside
theses.subtitle: India, IturanMob in the US and data contracts are not in our numbers
points: IturanMob, a platform for small and mid-sized rental companies, is piloting in Orlando and New York after launching in Brazil.
The Mercedes-Benz commercial-vehicle joint venture in India is low-margin today but long-dated.
The September 2026 big-data traffic-monitoring contract shows that the subscriber data has value beyond recovery.
theses.risk: These projects eat margin without reaching scale. Management has called India a long-term, low-margin bet.

evidence.title: What our base case leaves out
points: Our DCF uses consensus growth of ~16% in 2026 and ~5% in 2027, fading to 2.5%. It does not assume any US or India success.
Any sign that IturanMob or the data business is gaining scale would be upside to the target.

theses.source: Ituran Q3 2025 earnings call; Ituran press release 9 Sep 2026; consensus via Yahoo Finance

comps.title: Ituran trades at a discount to connected-vehicle peers on every multiple
comps.subtitle: Despite a higher EBITDA margin than most of the group
comps.note: Peers: vehicle-telematics and connected-fleet platforms plus Garmin as a consumer-device leader.

dcf.subtitle: Consensus growth to 2027, fading to 2.5%; EBIT margin held near 21%; WACC raised one point for country risk

valuation.title: Nearly every method points above the share price
points: The target blends our DCF with the value implied by the peer-median EV/EBITDA. Too few peers had a usable P/E.
Analyst consensus targets ($69–80) sit above ours. The two covering analysts both rate the stock a Buy.

risks.title: Country risk is the main debate; the business itself is resilient

items.mitigant: A WACC one point higher than the model, net cash, and dollar reporting with a natural hedge across several currencies.

items.risk: Slower subscriber growth if OEM ramps slip
items.mitigant: A diversified base of 2.7m subscribers. Israel is mature but steady.

items.risk: Technology substitution by car makers' built-in connectivity
items.mitigant: OEM partnerships turn the threat into a channel: Ituran runs the service behind factory-fitted units.
